I am renting this 2.29-hectare plot in the highlands of Oromia, so I must make the barley yield well to pay the landlord and still have grain for my household. I will apply DAP and urea from the cooperative—about 50 kilograms of nitrogen per hectare—because the land needs fertilizer, and I will also spread manure on it since I keep livestock. I will sow my own traditional barley seed, not improved seed, because that is what I have saved and it is hard to find improved barley seed here. I will not spray chemicals or irrigate; we rely on the meher rains and hand-weeding for barley. My family will do most of the ploughing, planting, and harvesting, but I will hire extra hands for about twenty days during weeding and threshing since the plot is large and I have other fields to tend.
